text: I understand you are experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To begin my assessment, have you noticed any specific changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea, constipation, or blood in your stool, alongside the abdominal pain?

text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text:
The sensation of abdominal fullness with tighter clothes suggests significant organomegaly, likely hepatosplenomegaly. Given your B-symptoms (night sweats, weight loss), supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, and lack of respiratory symptoms, could you describe any pain in your right upper quadrant or left upper quadrant, and have you noticed any skin discoloration or yellowing of your eyes?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL). The presence of splenomegaly, B-symptoms, and a CD20-positive lymph node biopsy with a high proliferative index confirms a B-cell malignancy, most likely DLBCL given the aggressive clinical presentation.
